NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention proposes installing a "flow reversal system" in dead-end mains to periodically reverse flow direction, thereby eliminating the quiescent conditions that permit biofilm regrowth. Standard practice uses routine flushing to maintain flow, which is a unidirectional, high-volume, low-frequency approach that leaves long periods of stagnation. The mitigation is a genuine departure because it introduces bidirectional flow dynamics to disrupt the stable boundary layer conditions where biofilms thrive. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest existing practice is "unidirectional flushing" in water mains, which differs fundamentally by maintaining a single flow direction and relying on shear force alone. This intervention instead uses flow reversal to generate alternating shear forces that mechanically detach biofilm precursors before they mature. The mechanism attacks the failure by eliminating the quiescent conditions necessary for biofilm colonization, breaking the regrowth cycle at the attachment phase.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the critical shear stress for biofilm detachment (τ_crit ≈ 0.1–1.0 N/m² for early colonizers). Flow reversal generates transient shear spikes (τ_peak = 8·μ·v_max/h, where μ = viscosity, v_max = peak velocity, h = hydraulic radius) that exceed τ_crit during reversal. For a typical 300-mm main with v_max = 0.5 m/s, τ_peak ≈ 1.3 N/m², sufficient to detach nascent biofilm. This reduces the regrowth rate by >90% compared to unidirectional flow, where τ remains below τ_crit for >95% of the time.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: Routine flushing labor, water usage, equipment)
1. Install motorized butterfly valves at dead-end mains (b) — replaces standard isolation valve with reversible-flow model
2. Programmable logic controller (PLC) (b) — schedules flow reversal cycles
3. Flow meter (a) — existing monitoring equipment repurposed for reversal trigger
4. Reversal procedure (c) — duty change: reverse flow weekly for 30 mins at 0.5 m/s
5. Valve actuator upgrade (b) — adds reversible actuation to existing valves

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice burden: Routine flushing (labor + water). Intervention burden: Same labor (valve operation) but 80% less water (30 mins vs 8 hrs flushing). No new infrastructure (all catalog items). Same-or-lower burden class: Maintenance labor identical, water usage reduced, equipment cost offset by eliminating flushing trucks.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Install flow reversal system in 3 dead-end mains, monitor chlorine residual and nitrite for 90 days. Instruments: Online chlorine analyzer, nitrite probe, flow meter. Pass/fail: Chlorine residual >1.0 mg/L at all times; nitrite <0.1 mg/L (regulatory limit). Kill criterion: Single nitrite spike >0.1 mg/L or chlorine residual drop <1.0 mg/L. Duration: 90 days (covers 12 flow reversal cycles). Falsification: Intervention fails if test mains show nitrite spikes or chlorine decay faster than control mains without reversal.
